prompt: What went wrong with lesson 12's `CourseListView` on a train with no signal?
hint: The phone had seen the courses that morning.

choices.text: It crashed on the `DecodingError`
choices.why: No body arrived to decode; the request failed before that.

choices.text: It showed an error, though nothing had changed
choices.why: Right: it asked the network every time, and nothing kept the courses it had already seen.

choices.text: It showed yesterday's courses with no warning that they were old
choices.why: It showed nothing old at all; it had kept nothing.

choices.text: It kept retrying and drained the battery
choices.why: Lesson 12's screen retries only when the person presses the button.

prompt: Why does `PlannerRepository` hold a `PlanSource` and a `PlanStore` rather than an `APIClient` and a `FileStore`?
hint: Think of the tests in section 06.

choices.text: Because actors cannot hold structs
choices.why: Actors hold structs; `snapshot` is one.

choices.text: To make the compiled app smaller on the phone
choices.why: Size is not the reason.

choices.text: So a test, or SwiftData later, stands in for either one
choices.why: Right: the repository is written against what they can do, not what they are.

choices.text: Because `APIClient` cannot be used inside an actor
choices.why: It can; it is `Sendable`, and it is the source in `repo`.

prompt: Which of these are promises the repository makes to the screens? Choose all that apply.
hint: Section 02 lists three.

choices.text: A read answers at once with what the device has
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A write waits until the server confirms it
choices.why: No: a write lands on the device first.

choices.text: A failed request never empties the device's plan
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The server never refuses a session the device accepted
choices.why: No: it can, and the repository reports it.

prompt: Why is `extension APIClient: PlanSource {}` empty?
hint: Compare the protocol with lesson 12's client.

choices.text: Its methods are added later, in section 04
choices.why: Nothing is added later; the conformance is complete.

choices.text: Protocols in Swift provide every method by default
choices.why: Only with a protocol extension, and `PlanSource` has none.

choices.text: It already has all three methods
choices.why: Right: the protocol is the client's signatures with the bodies removed.

choices.text: An empty extension marks `APIClient` as deprecated in favour of the repository
choices.why: Nothing is deprecated; the repository uses the client.

prompt: `FileStore.save` writes with `.atomic`. What does that protect against?
hint: What would an app killed mid-write leave behind?

choices.text: Half a file after a crash
choices.why: Right: it writes elsewhere and renames, so the old file stays whole until the new one is complete.

choices.text: Two screens saving at the same moment from different threads
choices.why: That is the actor's job; `.atomic` is about one write being whole.

choices.text: Another app reading the planner's file
choices.why: Other apps cannot reach it in the first place; that is the sandbox.

choices.text: A disk that is full
choices.why: A full disk still fails the write; `storeError` is what reports it.

prompt: The sessions added on the device that the server has not confirmed are kept in the snapshot's list called ___.
hint: It is the list `sync` walks.

prompt: A refresh gets the courses, then fails on the second course's sessions. What does the device's plan look like afterwards?
hint: Where does `refresh` assign to the snapshot?

choices.text: The new courses, and the first course's sessions only
choices.why: Nothing is assigned until every request has succeeded.

choices.text: Exactly as it was before the refresh
choices.why: Right: the `throw` leaves before the snapshot is touched.

choices.text: Empty, until the next refresh works
choices.why: Emptying the plan on a failure is what the repository exists to prevent.

choices.text: The new courses with no sessions
choices.why: The courses are not assigned either.

prompt: After the first successful refresh, how many minutes did the week of 19 October have planned?
hint: The server's four sessions, three of them in that week.

prompt: Why is `plan` a computed property of the actor and not an `async` function that asks the server?
hint: What would a screen wait for?

choices.text: Because actors cannot have `async` functions
choices.why: `refresh` and `sync` are `async` functions of the same actor.

choices.text: To avoid decoding JSON twice
choices.why: Decoding is not what it saves.

choices.text: Because SwiftUI cannot call an `async` function
choices.why: SwiftUI calls them from `task` and `refreshable`.

choices.text: So a read never waits for the network, whatever it is doing
choices.why: Right: reading is building a plan from two arrays already on the device.

prompt: `repo` run with no command printed `2 courses, 4 sessions` with the server stopped. Where did they come from?
hint: The previous run saved something.

choices.text: `planner.json`, saved by the last refresh
choices.why: Right: `PlannerRepository` loads the store when it is made.

choices.text: A cache inside `URLSession` that answered for the server
choices.why: `repo` with no command makes no request at all.

choices.text: The sample data written into `repo`'s `main.swift`
choices.why: `repo` has no sample data; the first run printed 0 courses.

choices.text: The server, which keeps running after `Ctrl-C` for a minute
choices.why: `Ctrl-C` stops it; the read came from the device.

prompt: Put what `add` does with a new session in order.
hint: Check, keep, save, send.
items: Check it against the plan the device has
Save the snapshot to the store
Call `sync`, which tries to send it

prompt: After `repo add s5` with the server stopped, how many minutes did the week have planned?
hint: The waiting session counts already.

prompt: `sync` gets `status(422, "no course art")` for a pending session. What does it do with it?
hint: Will the server ever accept it?

choices.text: Keeps it pending, to try again on the next sync
choices.why: A 4xx will not change; it would be sent for ever.

choices.text: Drops it and returns its id
choices.why: Right, so the screen can say what was not kept.

choices.text: Moves it to the confirmed sessions anyway
choices.why: The server refused it; calling it confirmed would be a lie.

choices.text: Creates the course `art` on the server and resends it
choices.why: The client has no way to create courses, and should not guess.

prompt: Match what came back to what `sync` does.
hint: Will trying again help?

pairs.right: Drops it and reports the id
Moves it to the confirmed sessions

prompt: Why can the repository's tests run without starting `serve.py`?
hint: What does the repository know about its source?

choices.text: Swift Testing starts a server for each test
choices.why: It starts nothing; the tests bring their own source.

choices.text: It is handed a `FakeSource` instead
choices.why: Right: anything that conforms will do.

choices.text: `URLSession` answers from a recorded file in tests
choices.why: No request is made at all.

choices.text: They skip every test that would need the network
choices.why: All eight ran and passed.

prompt: Why does each test make its own file with a fresh `UUID` in the name?
hint: Swift Testing runs tests at the same time.

choices.text: Because `FileStore` refuses to open a file twice
choices.why: It does not; two tests would happily share and break each other.

choices.text: To make the tests run faster
choices.why: Speed is not it.

choices.text: So parallel tests never read each other's plan
choices.why: Right: a shared file would make a test pass or fail by timing.

choices.text: Because the temporary directory is emptied after each test
choices.why: Nothing empties it between tests.

prompt: How many tests passed in section 06's run?
hint: Lesson 1, lesson 12 and this lesson.

prompt: In `FakeSource.add`, `loseNextAnswer` keeps the session and then throws `timedOut`. Which real situation is that?
hint: The server did the work.

choices.text: A phone with no signal at all
choices.why: Then the server would not have kept it; that is the `online` switch.

choices.text: A server that refuses an unknown course
choices.why: That is the 422 path, with no session kept.

choices.text: A request that arrived and was done, whose answer never got back
choices.why: Right: the phone cannot tell it from a request that never arrived.

choices.text: A request cancelled by the screen
choices.why: Cancelled is its own case; this is a timeout after the work was done.

prompt: What makes it safe for `sync` to send a session a second time after a timeout?
hint: It is a rule on the server.

choices.text: `URLSession` deduplicates repeated `POST` requests
choices.why: It sends what it is given.

choices.text: The server keeps a repeated id once
choices.why: Right: the id is made on the device, so the second post is recognisably the same session.

choices.text: The repository waits long enough for the first answer
choices.why: The first answer will never come; waiting cannot fix it.

choices.text: The timeout cancels the first request on the server
choices.why: Lesson 12's log showed the server finishing requests the client had abandoned.

prompt: An operation that gives the same result however many times it is repeated is called ___.
hint: The server's half of offline-first.

prompt: `repo add s6 art …` printed `not added: unknownCourse("art")`. Which code refused it?
hint: It happened before anything was saved or sent.

choices.text: The server, with a 422
choices.why: A 422 would come back as a refused id from `sync`, not as a `PlanError`.

choices.text: `FileStore`, which checks course ids on save
choices.why: The store saves whatever it is given.

choices.text: Lesson 1's `Plan.add`
choices.why: Right: the repository checks a write against the plan before keeping it.

choices.text: `APIClient.add`, before sending
choices.why: The client sends what it is given and reports what came back.

prompt: Why does the repository record `storeError` instead of using `try?` on `save`?
hint: What would the person be told otherwise?

choices.text: Because `try?` does not compile inside an actor
choices.why: It compiles anywhere.

choices.text: Silence would claim a session was saved
choices.why: Right: a silent failure here loses the person's work without a word.

choices.text: To retry the save automatically on the next launch
choices.why: Nothing retries it; it is reported.

choices.text: Because a failed save would also fail the network request
choices.why: The two are independent.

prompt: In `PlannerModel.refresh`, why is `show()` called before the repository's refresh?
hint: Section 04's promise.

choices.text: Because `refresh` throws away the plan
choices.why: A refresh that fails changes nothing.

choices.text: To draw the device's plan first
choices.why: Right: the screen is never empty while it waits.

choices.text: To cancel any earlier refresh
choices.why: `show` only reads; cancelling is `task`'s job.

choices.text: Because SwiftUI requires one read before every write
choices.why: There is no such rule.

prompt: What does `refreshable` add to the list in `CourseListView`?
hint: A gesture people already know.

choices.text: A button in the toolbar
choices.why: It adds a gesture, not a button.

choices.text: A timer that refreshes every minute
choices.why: Nothing runs on a timer.

choices.text: Pull to refresh, with the system's spinner
choices.why: Right: the spinner shows while the closure runs.

choices.text: A background refresh when the app is closed
choices.why: That is lesson 16, and it is not `refreshable`.

prompt: On the train, a student adds a session, closes the app, and opens it at home on Wi-Fi. Trace what the repository does, in order. Which is right?
hint: The file survives the app closing.

choices.text: Loads the file with the pending session, shows it, refreshes, and `sync` sends it
choices.why: Right: the pending list was saved before the app closed.

choices.text: Starts empty, since pending sessions live only in memory
choices.why: `pending` is in the snapshot, and the snapshot is saved on every change.

choices.text: Refreshes first, and the refresh deletes the pending session
choices.why: A refresh replaces the server's half and leaves `pending` alone.

choices.text: Asks the student whether to send the session
choices.why: Sending is automatic; asking would be a question nobody can answer well.

choices.text: The four repository tests

choices.text: `PlannerModel` and `CourseListView` with `refreshable`
